parsed.why: No documented trans-specific criminalisation, targeting, border friction, or facility restriction. Social acceptance and trans-specific protections are not established; dated anti-LGB hostility and weak responses to homophobic attacks modestly lower confidence and safety.

Strong current protections and marriage equality help, but a recent mob attack on trans people and documented police mistreatment show real hostility. The reported arrests and available custody-transfer route provide some, but incomplete, reassurance.

Criminal provisions are actively used against gender-nonconforming people: a trans woman received an eight-year sentence and was held in a men's prison. Arbitrary arrests, police abuse, and hostile institutions make outing exceptionally dangerous.

No trans-specific criminalisation and formal protections coexist with recent allegations of police assault and sexual harassment, repeated attacks without sanctions, and significant hostility. These documented, poorly remedied exposures outweigh paper protections.

Current visitor-facing protections include gender-congruent facilities, anti-discrimination rules, and hate-crime coverage, alongside documented social acceptance. The proposed rollback remains at first reading and chiefly concerns residents' legal recognition, not visitors' documents.
